question: Which of the following molecules has single covalent bond?
solution:
The correct answer is **__H₂__.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **H₂** consists of two hydrogen atoms sharing a single pair of electrons, forming a single covalent bond.
 
• Each hydrogen atom in H₂ has one electron, and they share this pair to achieve a stable electron configuration.
 
• The single covalent bond in H₂ is a sigma (σ) bond, which is the strongest type of covalent bond.
 
• This bond formation allows each hydrogen atom to achieve the electron configuration of helium, which is a stable noble gas configuration.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Covalent Bond**

 
 
• A covalent bond involves the sharing of electron pairs between atoms.
 
• These bonds can be single, double, or triple, depending on the number of electron pairs shared.
 
• Covalent bonds are typically found in molecules with nonmetal atoms.
 
 
 
• **Single Covalent Bond**
 
 
• A single covalent bond involves one pair of shared electrons.
 
• Single covalent bonds are represented by a single line between the bonded atoms in molecular diagrams.
 
• Examples include H₂, Cl₂, and CH₄ (methane).
 
 
 
• **Double and Triple Covalent Bonds**
 
 
• Double covalent bonds involve two pairs of shared electrons (e.g., O₂).
 
• Triple covalent bonds involve three pairs of shared electrons (e.g., N₂).
 
• These bonds are stronger and shorter than single covalent bonds.
 
 
 
• **Noble Gas Configuration**
 
 
• Atoms form covalent bonds to achieve a stable electron configuration similar to noble gases.
 
• Noble gases have a complete outer electron shell, making them chemically inert.
 
• Hydrogen achieves the electron configuration of helium when it forms a single covalent bond.
